title: Mum's Youngest (Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm female vocal 100bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling intimate unhurried
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The youngest one grows up watching two ahead
He learned from every move they made
But Joel always had his own direction
A quieter path, a different kind of brave

[Verse 2]
He went to Zimbabwe, came home with Kerri
I said — son, is this the one? He just smiled
She's from a farm, her parents Jeff and Jill
And now they have a daughter who can sing like wild

[Chorus]
My youngest one, the one who went the furthest
My youngest one, the one who found his first
Ari's got a voice that stops the morning
My youngest one — I always knew you'd learn

[Bridge]
He rang me from the hospital once
Said Mum, Jack got me on the golf buggy bad
I said — Joel, that is not how you drive a golf buggy
He said — Mum, I wasn't driving, Jack was — I was just too glad

[Verse 3]
He makes the songs now, sends them round the group
The family all around the phone
His Oma's voice is somewhere in his singing
That's how you know — he was never alone

[Outro]
The gardens still growing
The gardens still growing
My youngest one
The gardens still growing
